children: Top European natural gas supplier Equinor

said Wednesday it aims to expand its liquefied natural gas supply portfolio to 10M-15M metric tons/​year by the early 2030s to meet demand from Europe ‌and Asia, and it expects to announce a second deal to supply LNG to an Asian customer this week.
"We have ⁠been in dialogue with many counterparties, especially in India and also places ​in Southeast Asia, wanting to have new sources," Equinor
LNG VP Ingvar Egeland told Reuters, adding that the company ​focuses on supply deals to state energy companies and fertilizer producers.
Egeland said potential ​sources of new supply include the east coast of the U.S., the west coast of Canada, ​South America, and Tanzania and other African countries.

The Middle East war has prevented Qatar and the United Arab Emirates from exporting most of their LNG through ​the Strait of Hormuz, where ~20% of global supplies used to ​pass, forcing Asian buyers to seek other supplies.

European natural gas prices have nearly tripled YTD, with the Dutch TTF benchmark trading near €81/MWh, as traders are looking for more clarity on gas purchases from Germany - Europe's biggest energy market - whose inventories are abnormally low.

With the next heating season approaching, the European gas market is more exposed to supply disruptions and renewed price volatility, as European Union gas inventories are ~68% full, significantly below the 84% five-year average; in Germany, the level is just 56%.

European gas could approach €100/MWh this winter given sustained disruptions to Middle East supplies and Europe’s historically low storage levels, Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Patricio Alvarez said in a note.

for October delivery rose 0.5% to $2.936/MMBtu, while crude oil futures took a breather after rallying to nearly four-month highs, as front-month Nymex crude
